info.title: Hub REST API
info.summary: REST surface of the hub (Home Assistant app).
info.description: Snapshot of the FastAPI schema of the hub 2026.12.0, annotated by tools/snapshot_openapi.py. All routes live under /api, there is no version prefix. The WebSocket /api/ws is described in asyncapi/hub-ws.asyncapi.yaml. Errors use FastAPI's {"detail": ...}. Unknown GET paths (also below /api) are answered by the SPA fallback with 200 text/html instead of 404. Cookie and header names are functional; namespace-dependent names follow namespace.json (halumar).

LAN, TLS with self-signed leaf; clients pin the SHA-256 fingerprint (Bonjour fp, QR fp, client_config)

post.description:
Login with Home Assistant credentials.

Validates username/password against the HA Auth API via Supervisor proxy.
On success, sets a session cookie for web UI access. Only while direct
admin access is switched on (default off): otherwise 403 with reason
``admin_ingress_only`` before the credentials are checked.

Rate limited: 5 attempts per IP per minute; 5 failures per account and
address in 15 minutes; an account is blocked as a whole only after 30
failures from at least 5 addresses.

Logout - destroy session and clear cookie.

A valid session is only ended with its CSRF token, like every
other state-changing request of the session.

get.description:
Check if the current session is valid.

Returns session info if authenticated, otherwise {authenticated: false,
direct_access} and, with direct access off, ha_url (Home Assistant in
the home network, or null). The frontend shows the login page or the
"only through Home Assistant" page.

Check if an API token exists (does NOT return the actual token).

The token is only shown once when generated/regenerated.
This endpoint just confirms a token exists.
Admin-only: paired clients cannot access this endpoint.

post.description:
Regenerate the API token. Returns the new token ONCE.

The token is only shown at this moment - it cannot be retrieved again.
Store it securely. All external clients using the old token will lose access.
The token is stored as a SHA-256 hash in the database.
Admin-only: paired clients cannot access this endpoint.

get.description:
Report whether an integration token exists (never returns the token).

``supervisor_managed`` tells the UI that the token is rotated and
delivered automatically on every hub start (discovery), so manual
copying is only needed when it is False. Admin-only.

post.description:
Rotate the integration token. Returns the new token ONCE.

Invalidates the previous integration token immediately; a configured
integration keeps failing (counted + logged) until it is reconfigured —
or, under the Supervisor, until the next hub start re-announces the
then-current token via discovery. Admin-only.

post.description:
Import areas from exported data. Admin-only.

Every entry is validated first (same rules as ``POST /areas``
limits); invalid entries are reported and skipped. The import runs in ONE
transaction, each area in its own savepoint: concurrent writes wait, a
failing area is rolled back alone, and a database error rolls back the
whole import (503, nothing imported, safe to retry). If no entry could be
imported because all of them were invalid, the answer is 422.

schema.title: Response Import Areas Api Import Areas Post

get.description:
Full status snapshot for the Halumar integration.

Contains device names, owners and current areas; never tokens or
notification texts.

Returns everything the integration needs in a single call:
- Hub info (version, area count, connected clients)
- All areas with their status
- All paired clients with their current status + connection state;
  notifications appear as ids+counts only (never title/message/action);
  platform and set_up_by tell the integration which device shows a
  watch's notifications while the hub is down
- Guests reduced to client_id/is_connected/expires_at
- pairing_active (+ non-secret window metadata; the PIN itself is NOT
  in this payload — the pairing-qr endpoint carries it)

The HA integration's DataUpdateCoordinator calls this endpoint
periodically (e.g. every 30s) to update all entities at once.
Integration-token only.

Rule snapshots of all devices with an HA user.

The complete set the integration applies when the hashes of the status
poll differ from its own (backstop for a lost ``enforcement_rules``
push). Integration-token only.

post.description:
Kids counter and pause before an action.

The integration asks before executing a kids action whose entity has a
rate limit; an allowed action is counted. A ``grant`` the hub passed
itself in ``<ns>.control`` is answered allowed without counting twice.
Integration-token only.

A Home Assistant admin or an automation turned a device's access
switch (``switch.<ns>_<name>_access``). 404 unknown device, 409
``no_access_switch``. Integration-token only.

The integration accepted a ``<ns>.report_location`` of a device:
whether and how it shares its location, never the position. 404 unknown
device, 422 invalid ts. Integration-token only.

Integration events for the log tab. Idempotent per event id.

Data minimization: ids, entity, action name, route, origin, reason,
counts and times only. Integration-token only.

Accept the token of a device's own HA user. Idempotent.

The integration created (or rotated) the HA user's token after a
provision_client request and delivers it here. The token is stored
encrypted and the connected app is told to fetch its new config; only
then does the integration remove the previous token (after this 200).

404 ``client_not_found`` and 409 ``client_inactive`` make the integration
remove the HA user; 503 ``db_unavailable`` makes it retry with the same
token. The bearer is never logged or returned. Integration-token only.

External Home Assistant URL as HA reports it.

The integration asks HA (``get_url`` without internal URLs: its
``external_url``, else the Home Assistant Cloud address) and reports the
result here when it changes, also when the cloud connection or HA's
configuration changes; null = none. It becomes ``ha_url_detected`` and,
unless the admin set another external URL in the hub, the URL devices
with remote access get in ``client_config``.

Only a URL equal to HA's ``external_url`` (read by the hub from the
Supervisor) or a Home Assistant Cloud address is accepted (422
``url_not_allowed``), so the integration token cannot send the devices'
HA tokens elsewhere. Connected apps are told to fetch their config when
the URL changes. Integration-token only.

``ha_instance_id`` (HA's instance ID) is stored and handed to the
devices as ``client_config.ha_instance_id``: when the pinned hub does not
answer, an HA announced over Bonjour with this ``uuid`` confirms the home
network for unencrypted HA addresses. A change also counts as ``changed``.

get.description:
Return the image of the integration's pairing camera entity.

Every HA user and every device token can read a camera entity. The QR
code with the pairing deep link (and so the PIN) is therefore shown only
when the admin switched it on with the app option ``pairing_qr_camera``:
``guests`` during a guest pairing window,
``all`` during every window, and only to an integration that sends
``X-Pairing-Qr: accept``. Then ``X-Pairing-Pin: included``,
``X-Pairing-Kind: guest|device`` and ``X-Pairing-Window`` (an opaque id
of the window, not derived from the PIN). Otherwise a status image ("PAIRING" /
"STANDBY", with a line why no QR is shown) and ``X-Pairing-Pin:
omitted``. Never cached: once the window ends or the PIN is used the
next request gets the status image. Integration-token only.

200.description: PNG of the integration's pairing camera. A status image (PAIRING / STANDBY, with a line why no QR is shown) and X-Pairing-Pin: omitted, unless the hub option pairing_qr_camera allows the open window (guests: guest windows only, all: every window; reported as pairing_qr_camera in GET /api/integration/status): then the QR of the canonical pairing deep link (contains the PIN), X-Pairing-Pin: included and X-Pairing-Kind. Never cached; after the window ends or the PIN is used the next request gets the status image.

X-Pairing-Pin.description: included = the image is the QR with the PIN; omitted = a status image without it.

X-Pairing-Kind.description: Only with X-Pairing-Pin: included. guest = a guest pairing window (the PIN only creates a guest with the profile and end fixed when the window opened); device = any other window.

X-Pairing-Window.description: Only with X-Pairing-Pin: included. Opaque id of the pairing window (not derived from the PIN); the integration ends a camera stream when it changes.

parameters.name: X-Pairing-Qr
parameters.description: accept = the integration can show the QR code (it checks pairing_qr_camera and never caches it). Without it the hub always sends the status image and writes no audit entry.

get.description:
Device registry data for the HA custom integration.

Returns the device definitions that the integration should create
in the HA device registry, including identifiers, names, and
manufacturer info. Called once during integration setup and when
new devices are discovered.

Device types:
- hub: The Halumar hub itself (1 device)
- client: One device per paired client
Integration-token only.

post.description:
Start a pairing session (optionally for guests).

Accepts an optional JSON body (contracts integration/start-pairing.request):
- is_guest: bool (default false)
- guest_expires_hours: int (default: house setting, max 2160)
- guest_expires_at: ISO 8601 with offset (precedence over hours)
- guest_tags: list[str] (guests: areas as a device adjustment; missing =
  the profile decides; 409 rule_fixed when the profile fixes areas)
- profile: str (profile NAME; missing = default profile of the device type)
- owner_label: str (optional owner of the device, max 50 characters)
Integration-token only.

Blocked with 403 (user AND guest starts) when the admin disabled the
allow_pairing_via_integration setting; cancel stays available.
Set an area's is_active to true. Used by HA switch entities. Integration-token only.
Set an area's is_active to false. Used by HA switch entities. Integration-token only.

Navigate a client to a specific area.

Body: {"area_id": "uuid"} or {"area_id": "__home__"} (HOME screen).
The client UI will switch to display the specified area.
Integration-token only.

Show an entity on a client, regardless of whether it belongs to an area.

Body: {"entity_id": "light.living_room", "control_mode": "full"}
The client will display a detail view for this entity.
control_mode is optional (basic/advanced/full) and tells the client
which level of controls to show for this entity.
Integration-token only.

Panel command from Home Assistant.

The integration calls it from its panel entities after checking the
caller (HA admin or automation, never a device user). The hub checks the
device (panel, not a guest, rule panel_remote, platform), sends the
WebSocket command panel_command and waits up to 5 s for the app's answer.
Errors: {"detail": {"code", "message"}} with 404/422/504. Every command is
logged with its actor. Integration-token only.

Send a notification to one client or broadcast to all.

Body matches POST /api/notifications (the hub's notification model):
client_id is a paired-client id or "all" (broadcast to every active
client except watches), plus title/message/notification_type/icon/
popup_mode/scheduled_at/priority/color/action_type/action_target/show_time,
and an optional ``notification_id`` (UUID chosen by the integration) that
makes a retried call idempotent. With "all" it is a broadcast id: every device's
notification gets UUIDv5(broadcast id, client id) and devices that
already have theirs are skipped.

A notification for a watch goes to the phone that set it up, the answer
names it in ``forwarded_to`` (422 when that phone is no longer paired);
an idempotent id is compared against that phone.

Returns {"sent": N} for the "all" broadcast (plus ``duplicates`` with a
broadcast id), otherwise {"notification": ..., "ws_sent": ...} (plus
``duplicate: true`` when the id already existed). Integration-token only.

422.description: Validation Error, or the target is a watch whose phone (the device that set it up) is deleted, inactive or being deleted: detail as text, nothing stored.

post.description:
Take over notifications the integration queued while the hub was down.

While the hub is unreachable, the integration writes notifications
directly into the client's notification sensor (with its own UUIDs) and
hands them over here once the hub answers again; from then on the hub is
the source of truth. Per item:

- unknown id -> created with the given ``notification_id``/``created_at``
  (``created``); ``status: "delivered"`` (the app confirmed it through
  Home Assistant meanwhile) is stored as delivered via 'remote' and not
  pushed again, a pending one is pushed to the connected app;
- id of the same client already known -> ``duplicates`` (idempotent);
- an item for a watch goes to the phone that set it up, like a live
  notification (``client_not_found`` when that phone is gone);
- unknown client, id of another client, invalid content or older than
  72 h -> ``skipped`` with a reason.

The notification sensors are rewritten once at the end (always, since
the integration wrote them meanwhile). Integration-token only.

Disconnect a client's WebSocket session(s).

The client row stays active — this only drops the live connection(s);
the client may reconnect with its existing secret. Close code 4004 is
deliberately NOT one of the reset codes the apps act on (4001 = removed,
4002 = auth timeout, 4003 = guest expired), so a kick never wipes
credentials. Use the client management API to deactivate/delete a client
for good. Returns 200 with closed=0 when the client is offline.
Integration-token only.

Cancel any open pairing window.

Idempotent: returns 200 also when no pairing window is open
(cancelled=false in that case). Integration-token only.

Clear all notifications on a client (sticky, normal, and permanent).

No body required. Dismisses all in DB and sends clear command via WS.
Returns success even if client is offline (DB state is authoritative).
Integration-token only.

Remote fallback ack: mark notifications as delivered on a client's behalf.

When a client app can reach only Home Assistant (the hub is reachable
only on the home network and the app is away), it reads its notifications from the per-client HA
sensor and confirms them through the ``halumar.ack_notifications`` HA
service; the integration forwards the batch here. This is the
write-scope-minimal remote counterpart of the WS ``notification_ack``
(remote dismiss is deliberately NOT exposed).

Per id, the same ownership rule as the WS path applies: ids that are
unknown, belong to another client, or are no longer pending go silently to
``skipped`` (which also makes a duplicate/racing ack idempotent); matching
pending ids are acknowledged with ``delivered_via='remote'``.

For each acked id an ADMIN ``notification_delivered`` broadcast
(data: notification_id/client_id/via="remote") is emitted, and the HA
notification sensors are synced exactly ONCE per call (only when at least
one id was acked) so the sensor flips to delivered for the app's next
poll. Unknown client → 404, deactivated client → 422.

Response: 200 {"success": true, "client_id": ..., "acked": [...],
"skipped": [...]}. Integration-token only.

Force a client to reload all area and entity data.

No body required.
Integration-token only.

Set the areas of a device from the integration's tag list.

Body: {"tags": ["kitchen", "guests"]}: the FULL new list. It becomes a
device adjustment of the rule ``areas`` (``["*"]`` = all areas, ``[]`` =
all for members, none for guests; ``area:<id>`` = one area). 409
``rule_fixed`` when the profile fixes ``areas``. Integration-token only.

Extend a guest client's session expiry.

Body: {"hours": 2.5} (adds N hours from now) or {"expires_at": "ISO"}
(explicit new expiry, seconds truncated). Only guest clients can be
extended (400 otherwise). Delegates to extend_guest_expiry (shared with
the admin PATCH /clients/{id}/extend) and returns the same payload
(``dry_run`` included). Integration-token only.

get.description:
List notifications across all clients.

Query params:
  - status: "active" (default, pending+delivered), "all" (include dismissed)

Admin-only.

post.description:
Create and send a notification to a client.

Body: {
    "client_id": "uuid",            // or "all" (every device except watches)
    "title": "Alert",
    "message": "Something happened",
    "notification_type": "normal",  // "normal", "sticky", "permanent"
    "icon": "mdi:bell"              // optional
}

Creates the notification in the DB, then sends it to the client via
WebSocket if connected. Broadcasts notification_created to admin UIs.

A watch has no hub connection: a notification for a watch goes to the
phone that set it up (its system shows it on the watch while the phone is
locked); the response names that phone in ``forwarded_to`` and is 422
when that phone is no longer paired.

When ``client_id`` is "all", the notification is created and delivered to
every active paired client except watches (they get it through their
phone); the response is a summary ({"sent": N}).

popup_mode "direct" immediately opens the linked area/entity/url on the
client and therefore REQUIRES an action (action_type != "none" with an
action_target).

Admin-only.

422.description: Validation Error, or the target is a watch whose phone (the device that set it up) is deleted, inactive or being deleted: detail as text, nothing stored.

Only accessible via Ingress (admin) or with API token.

get.description:
List all paired clients with live connection status. Admin-only.

Hidden tombstones are background-only markers (kept so a returning app
is still reset on reconnect): they are not listed.

schema.title: Response List Paired Clients Api Pairing Clients Get

delete.description:
Delete ALL paired clients (both regular and guest). Admin-only.

Disconnects all active WebSocket connections and removes all clients from DB.
This is a destructive operation — all pairing data is permanently lost.

get.description: Get a single paired client by ID. Admin-only.

patch.description:
Update a paired client's name or owner label. Admin-only.

A change is reported to the integration (update_client_identity), which
renames the device's HA user.

delete.description:
Revoke (block) a paired client at once. Admin-only.

For a lost or stolen device: the row stays as "revoked" (the app gets
``auth_error`` reason ``revoked``), live connections close and the
device's HA user is removed now. Removing the row afterwards is a normal
delete (``DELETE …/permanent``, then the tombstone).

get.description: Activity feed of one device, newest first. Admin-only.

put.description:
Turn a device's access switch on or off. Admin-only.

The same switch Home Assistant shows as ``switch.<ns>_<name>_access``.
409 ``no_access_switch`` when the device has none.

get.description:
Whether an area is assigned/visible to a client. Admin-only.

Returns ``{"visible": bool}`` using the canonical assignment rule:
area has no tags OR client has no tags OR their tag sets overlap.

This is a VIEW/assignment check (does the area appear in the client's
area list). It does NOT reflect control authorization, which is enforced
per-entity at call_service time. A deep-linked notification area can be
opened by any client even when ``visible`` is False; this endpoint lets the
Web-UI surface the assignment state (e.g. badge/warning) for an admin.

delete.description:
Delete a paired client and force its app to reset. Admin-only.

Returns instantly. Order:
  1. Mark the row pending-deletion (``pending_deletion_at`` set,
     ``is_active=0``). The row is NOT hard-deleted here.
  2. Signal any LIVE connection of this client to reset itself
     (``client_removed`` over its live WS). The app wipes locally and
     replies with ``client_reset_ack`` ("wiped"), which purges the
     tombstone; a connection that never acks is force-closed (4001) after
     a short grace period WITHOUT purging. We do NOT close the socket or
     delete the row here.
  3. The device's HA user is held (``ha_user_holds`` in the status
     snapshot) until the app confirmed the reset or a grace period ran
     out, then the integration removes it (``deprovision_client``).
     Removing the user first made HA close the app's session before it
     knew it was removed, or made a returning offline app fail
     its first HA login. Online the grace period is the reset-ack
     window (``RESET_ACK_GRACE_SECONDS``); an offline device keeps its
     user until its app comes back (the hub replays ``client_removed``)
     or at most ``DELETE_HOLD_SECONDS``, unless the admin chose
     ``ha_user_removal=immediate`` (default for devices with remote
     access). Revoke removes it at once.
  4. Return 204.

204 means the deletion took effect: the device can no longer control
anything, a connected app is told to reset, and its HA user goes as
described above. It does not mean the row is gone: the row stays
as a tombstone and the list shows it with ``pending_deletion: true``
("Waiting for device") until the app confirms its reset. A connected
device confirms within moments, so it leaves the list at once; an offline
one stays listed until it returns, also with ``ha_user_removal=immediate``
(that choice only decides when the HA user goes). This is intended: only
the tombstone lets a returning app wipe itself.

The signed tombstone (client_id + secret_hash) persists INDEFINITELY until
the device's authenticated LAN wipe-ack arrives (reconnect replays the
``client_removed`` handshake), so the compliance endpoint keeps returning a
signed "deleted" for it. To take it off the list without losing that,
POST /clients/{id}/dismiss-pending hides it; an admin can force-purge via
DELETE /pairing/clients/{id}/tombstone.

parameters.name: ha_user_removal

schema.description: Only for a device that is offline when deleted: 'on_reconnect' keeps its HA user until the app confirms its reset on return (max. 24 h, clean return to setup); 'immediate' removes the HA user now (the tombstone stays and is listed as pending deletion; the app is still reset on return). Default: 'immediate' for devices with remote access, 'on_reconnect' for home-network-only devices. Ignored while the device is connected (reset-ack window).
schema.title: Ha User Removal

parameters.description: Only for a device that is offline when deleted: 'on_reconnect' keeps its HA user until the app confirms its reset on return (max. 24 h, clean return to setup); 'immediate' removes the HA user now (the tombstone stays and is listed as pending deletion; the app is still reset on return). Default: 'immediate' for devices with remote access, 'on_reconnect' for home-network-only devices. Ignored while the device is connected (reset-ack window).

post.description:
Hide a pending-deletion tombstone from the clients list. Admin-only.

Only valid for a client that is currently pending-deletion
(``pending_deletion_at`` set). Sets ``pending_hidden_at`` so the row is
excluded from the clients list, but does NOT delete the row: the tombstone
persists as a background marker so a returning app is still rejected (4001)
on reconnect and only then removed.

delete.description:
Force-purge a pending-deletion tombstone. Admin-only.

Escape hatch for a device that never returns: hard-deletes the tombstone
row (client_id + secret_hash), after which the compliance endpoint stops
signing "deleted" for it and serves the neutral "unknown". Only valid for
a client that is pending-deletion (400 otherwise). The normal purge path
stays the device's authenticated LAN wipe-ack (``client_reset_ack``).

get.description:
Get current pairing status. Admin-only.

Returns whether a PIN is active and how many paired clients exist.
The PIN itself is only returned for Ingress (admin) requests.

delete.description: Cancel the currently active pairing PIN. Admin-only.

get.description: Running onboarding sessions (devices waiting to be set up). Admin-only.

delete.description: Cancel a running onboarding session. Admin-only.

get.description: Open guest invitations of member devices (never the PIN). Admin-only.

delete.description: Cancel an open guest invitation; the member gets ``revoked``. Admin-only.

get.description:
Get global HA URL settings. Admin-only.

Returns both the configured URLs and the auto-detected URLs from HA.
If no manual override is set, the auto-detected URL is used.

put.description:
Update global HA URL settings. Admin-only.

Empty string resets to auto-detected value (removes manual override).
These URLs are returned to the paired clients via get_client_config (the
external one only to devices with remote access); connected clients are
told to fetch it. A value that is not an http(s) URL (or carries
credentials, a query or a fragment) is refused with 422.

get.description:
Get the configured app URL. Admin-only.

The app URL is the base URL under which Halumar is reachable externally.
Used for QR codes, image URLs sent to clients, and mDNS TXT records.
If not set, auto-detection from request headers is used as fallback.

put.description:
Update the app URL setting. Admin-only.

Empty string clears the setting (reverts to auto-detection).
The change takes effect immediately for QR codes and image URLs.
put.x-known-deviation: Known deviation D11 (docs/protocol.md): no client_config_updated broadcast, no URL validation.

get.description: Get global default control mode. Admin-only.

put.description:
Update global default control mode. Admin-only.

This is the fallback used by the apps when neither the entity
nor the area has a control_mode override.

get.description: Get whether pairing can be started via the integration. Admin-only.

put.description:
Update whether pairing can be started via the integration. Admin-only.

When disabled, POST /api/integration/start-pairing returns 403 for both
user and guest pairings (the web UI stays the only pairing surface);
cancelling an open window via the integration remains allowed.

get.description: Get whether the compliance endpoint is enabled. Admin-only.

put.description:
Update whether the compliance endpoint is enabled. Admin-only.

When disabled, GET /api/integration/status omits all per-client
compliance blobs and tombstones, and the integration's unauthenticated
compliance view serves the neutral "unknown" body for every client.

get.description: Whether admins may also log in directly in the home network. Admin-only.

put.description:
Switch direct admin access (HA login on :8100). Ingress only.

Off (the default): the login and every direct session are refused, the
admin page opens only in the Home Assistant sidebar. Switching off ends
all direct sessions and closes their admin sockets (4401). Paired apps,
the integration and the admin API token are not affected.

get.description:
Get home screen / app appearance settings. Admin-only.

Returns the home title, background image paths, and the auto-detected
HA location_name as a default reference.

put.description:
Update home screen title. Admin-only.

Empty string clears the title (will send null to clients).

post.description:
Upload a home screen background image. Admin-only.

image_type: 'bg_light' or 'bg_dark'
Accepts multipart form data with a 'file' field.

delete.description: Delete a home screen background image. Admin-only.

get.description:
All area tags (sorted, unique) for the tag choice of the rule
``areas``. Admin-only.

patch.description:
Extend a guest client's expiry time. Admin-only.

Either provide 'hours' (adds N hours from now) or 'expires_at'
(sets an explicit new expiry timestamp). Only works on guest clients.
Delegates to extend_guest_expiry (shared with the integration endpoint).

post.description:
Immediately disconnect and permanently delete a client. Admin-only.

Closes any active WebSocket connections (close code 4003 for guests,
4001 for regular clients) and removes the client from the database.
Works for both guest and regular clients.

The device signs itself off with its own secret.

REST twin of WS ``client_leave`` for a device without a hub socket:
a watch, directly over the pinned TLS port or
through its phone.
Bearer = the device's client secret (checked by the auth middleware, 401
otherwise); ``client_id`` must be that device (422). Removed like
``client_leave``: no tombstone, HA user removed by the integration,
``client_kicked {reason: left}``, audit ``client_left``.

Ask the integration for a new HA token of this device. Admin-only.

The rotation is stored first (it survives a hub restart).

- 200: the new token arrived within ``ROTATE_WAIT_SECONDS`` (the app was
  told via client_config_updated).
- 202 ``rotation_requested``: sent, the integration has not answered yet.
- 202 ``pending``: the integration is not connected; the rotation runs as
  soon as it is (``provisioning[]`` on its next poll, retry loop once its
  push session is up). Answered at once instead of blocking.
  Also for a device with remote access that is not connected to the hub
  (away): the rotation waits until it connects, at most
  ``ROTATION_DEFER_SECONDS``, so it is not locked out of Home Assistant
  on the road.
- 409: the device is not active or has no HA token yet.

202.description: Rotation stored and still running: status rotation_requested (sent to the integration) or pending (integration not connected).

409.description: Device not active or without an HA token yet.

get.description:
Return recent hub log lines (plain text, newest last). Admin-only.

Proxies the Supervisor ``/addons/self/logs`` endpoint and trims the
output to the last ``lines`` lines. If the Supervisor is unreachable the
error message is returned in the ``logs`` field so the UI can surface it.

post.description: Trigger a hub restart via the Supervisor. Admin-only.

get.description:
Return the current TLS state for the admin UI. Admin-only.

Exposes the hub's ``tls_enabled`` option, the external TLS port, the pinned
fingerprint, and a public cert summary. Never returns the private key or
its path. ``fingerprint``/``cert`` are ``None`` when no cert exists yet.

post.description:
Rotate the self-signed TLS cert and return the new fingerprint. Admin-only.

Adds the detected LAN IP to the cert SAN (127.0.0.1 is added by the service
itself, so loopback is skipped). Does NOT auto-restart: the running TLS
server keeps serving the old cert until the operator restarts the hub,
and every paired client must re-pair against the new fingerprint.

get.description: Progress of the setup assistant. Admin-only.

put.description: Store the progress of the setup assistant. Admin-only.

get.description:
Newest audit entries first (admin actions, admin requests, security
events) since the hub started. Admin-only.

All suggestions (gallery) with the profiles created from each.

Empty profile: catalog defaults, default fixed / user's choice.

delete.description: Delete a profile; devices move to ``replacement``.

post.description: Take over the newer version of the suggestion (only on request).
Profile from a device: its profile values with all its adjustments.

post.description:
Dry run: would the profile's kids rules allow this action now (or at ``at``)?

Without ``area_ids`` the areas the entity is placed in are used. Counters

Release a child device (no quiet hours/rate limit) for ``minutes`` or
until the end of its bedtime ("until tomorrow morning").

delete.description: "Lift pause": end a release and every running cooldown of the device.

post.description:
Control one entity as a device on the hub path (same as WS ``control``).

200 ``control_ok``, 403 ``rule_blocked`` / ``control_error``, 422/409/
502/503 ``control_error``.

Position of a device on the hub path without a hub socket (same
as WS ``location_report``). 200 ``location_report_ok``, 403/422/429
``location_report_error`` (429 with ``Retry-After``).

get.description: Children and HA notify targets of a family manager device.

put.description: Set the children (all or a selection) and the HA notify targets.

get.description: Overview: family managers, children, open requests, settings.
House settings of the family manager (requests, limits, activity).

Log entries, newest first. ``has_more`` = older entries exist (``before_id``).

``important`` = only alarms and the kinds marked important in the

Every entry of the filters (at most 20 000) for the CSV export.
``notify.*`` actions from Home Assistant and the eligible devices.

get.description: Early access requests (open and last 7 days) and running early accesses.

post.description: The admin answers an early access request (first answer wins).

delete.description:
End a running early access of a device now (the device closes again
when its access hours do not allow it).

get.description:
Health check endpoint (also the Supervisor watchdog target).

Includes process uptime and the number of currently connected
(authenticated) WebSocket clients for basic observability. Probes the
database: if it is not usable (closed, stuck, locked so writes fail) the
endpoint answers 503 instead of "ok", so the
Supervisor watchdog can restart the hub.

Serve immutable assets with long-term cache headers.

Outside Ingress, JS/CSS go out gzip-compressed (services/static_compress).

Serve static files or SPA fallback for client-side routing.

Order:
1. Validate path stays within static_dir (prevent path traversal)
2. Try exact file match (e.g. areas.html for /areas)
3. Fall back to index.html for SPA routing (e.g. /areas/<uuid>)

All HTML responses include Cache-Control: no-cache to ensure browsers
always fetch the latest version (which references content-hashed JS/CSS).

instead of creating a second one. With client_id "all" it is a broadcast
id: each device's notification gets the id UUIDv5(broadcast id, client
id), and devices that already have it are skipped.
